title: Permission-surface redesign and evidence automation sprint plan
body:
Purpose and scope:

This working plan describes a pragmatic redesign of Redwood's permission surface and an automated evidence pipeline to support audit/SOC requirements and SIEM ingestion. It focuses on three deliverables for the next 10 weeks: (1) a decomposed RBAC v2 permission model with attribute-aware scoping; (2) a compact, SIEM-friendly audit schema and export path; (3) an evidence automation flow that produces tamper-evident compliance bundles for quarterly audits and ad-hoc evidence requests.

Principles guiding the design:
- Minimal blast radius: keep high-level roles coarse, move fine-grained control into capability tokens and attribute filters.
- Deterministic authorization: every decision must be reproducible given the request, policy version, and attestable inputs.
- Audit-first instrumentation: events emitted during authorization should be complete and compact for SIEM.
- Incremental rollout: shadow-mode then gradual enforcement with clear fallbacks.

Permission model overview (proposal):
1) Role + capability separation: users retain coarse roles (admin, platform, dev, support) for UX, while authorization decisions use a graph of capability tokens (e.g., model.read, model.deploy, dataset.provision). Capability tokens are composable and reference resource templates.
2) Attribute-scoped grants: grants attach attribute predicates (e.g., env == "prod" && org == "payments") implemented as normalized key/value pairs. Predicates are evaluated by the policy engine against request attributes and resource metadata.
3) Delegation and temporary elevation: introduce "delegate grants" with expiry and an audit handle. Delegation requests create ephemeral capability tokens with a parent grant id and an automated attestation entry.
4) Policy versioning: all grant/policy changes must include a policy_version string; the decision log binds to that version.

Auth decision lifecycle (high-level):
- Request arrives with authentication principal and attributes.
- Capability resolution maps API route + verb to required capability tokens.
- Policy engine evaluates grants + attribute predicates + exception rules.
- Decision (allow/deny/allow-with-conditions) is returned along with matched grant ids and policy_version.

Audit log schema (compact, SIEM-oriented):
We propose a single-line JSON event (newline-delimited JSON file) with these fields. Each field below is required in the event payload emitted by the auth layer: 
- timestamp: ISO-8601 UTC
- event_type: string e.g., "auth_decision", "grant_change", "delegation_request"
- event_id: UUID v4
- actor_id: principal id (user/service)
- actor_roles: list of coarse roles (string array)
- actor_attributes: flattened list of attributes (key:value pairs)
- resource_type: short string (model, dataset, route)
- resource_id: canonical resource path (org/team/model:version)
- capability: token requested (model.deploy)
- decision: allow | deny | conditional
- matched_grants: list of grant ids (can be empty)
- policy_version: string
- rule_id: single rule id when applicable
- request_context: short map: ip, region, platform (flattened string)
- before_state_hash: short SHA256 hex (optional, for admin changes)
- after_state_hash: short SHA256 hex (optional)
- correlation_ids: list (trace id, request id)
- retention_hint: string (raw, pii-filtered)

Export path to SIEM:
- Emit events to internal kafka topic "auth.events.v2" and to durable S3 per-tenant for archival (s3://audit-archives/{tenant}/{YYYY}/{MM}/events.ndjson.gpg).
- Upstream SIEM (Splunk/Elastic) will ingest using a dedicated forwarder that pulls from the S3 prefix and from Kafka.
- To reduce SIEM noise, we will send a subset of derived events to external SIEM: aggregated policy-change events, critical denies (security_high), and delegation_elevations. Full per-request logs remain in internal archives with RBAC-protected access.

Evidence automation flow (what auditors want):
1) Evidence bundle composition: for each control request, produce a bundle containing: 
   - snapshot of relevant grants (policy_version)
   - signed list of decisions for a sample window (ndjson)
   - config blob for the policy engine binary and git commit
   - attestation statements linking actors to identity provider assertions
   - cryptographic manifest (GPG signature + SHA256 manifest)
2) Automation trigger points:
   - scheduled quarterly bundles per-tenant
   - on-demand bundles via support/ops ticket (JIRA evidence request)
3) Packaging and signing:
   - bundles built in an immutable builder pod, signed with a rotating key held in HSM/KMS.
   - bundles uploaded to s3://evidence-bundles/{tenant}/{YYYY}-{MM}-{DD}/{bundle-id}.tar.gz.sig
4) Evidence retention and access:
   - default retention 2 years encrypted at rest; longer retention for customers requiring it (contractual).
   - access requires dual-approval: compliance request + business owner approval.

Rollout plan and timeline (10-week sprint cadence):
Phase 0: Discovery & mapping (weeks 0-1)
- Inventory top 200 routes and map to proposed capability tokens.
- Gap analysis vs current grants.
- Stakeholders: SRE, Platform, Support, Legal.

Phase 1: Engine + schema implementation (weeks 2-5)
- Implement capability token layer in auth service (shadow-eval mode).
- Emit new compact audit events to Kafka and S3.
- Schema registry: publish event schema and validate producers.
- Deliverable: auth service in shadow with 100% event coverage.

Phase 2: Evidence builder + packaging (weeks 4-7)
- Build bundle builder job and signer integration with KMS/HSM.
- Implement requester API for on-demand bundles.
- Deliverable: automated quarterly bundle generation for a single tenant.

Phase 3: Pilot rollout & enforcement (weeks 6-9)
- Select pilot tenants (internal teams and one small customer) for staged enforcement.
- Run canary with 10% traffic with conditional allow & automated rollback hooks.
- Validate SIEM ingestion and alerting.

Phase 4: Global enforcement & cleanup (weeks 9-10)
- Flip enforcement flags for all non-legacy tenants.
- Run migration scripts to convert old grants into capability tokens where possible.
- Post-migration audit and runbook update.

Safety nets and rollback mechanisms:
- Shadow mode with deterministic counter-factual logs.
- Automated rollback: if 5xx or auth-deny error rates increase beyond threshold for 10m, toggle enforcement to shadow for affected service.
- Emergency bypass: short-lived org-level bypass tokens with additional audit obligations and immediate alerting to SecOps.

Telemetry & KPIs to monitor:
- % of requests evaluated under v2 engine (target 100% by week 5).
- False-deny rate (manual triage) under pilot (target <0.1% of requests).
- Time-to-synthesize evidence bundle (SLA: 48h for on-demand).
- SIEM ingestion lag (goal <5m from event emission for high-priority events).
- Size of daily audit archive per tenant (for capacity planning).

Operational runbooks (short):
- How to generate an evidence bundle on-demand: confluence link (see linked_artifacts).
- How to inspect decision trace for a given request_id: use tooling auth-trace --id <request_id>.
- How to revoke a delegated token: revoke-grant --id <grant_id> and ensure immediate evict from cache.

Open questions / Known risks:
- Decision provenance for composite requests: how to present explainability when multiple services fan-out and each makes auth decisions? (proposal: propagate root trace_id and include service-level decisions in bundle).
- PII filtration: audit events include actor_attributes; need a consistent filter policy to avoid leaking email/SSN into external SIEM.
- KMS/HSM service-level SLA for signing: what happens during KMS outage? fallback key strategy required.
- Migration complexity for legacy grants that embed business logic in code rather than declarative grants.

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Run inventory script (security/infra team) to produce route->capability mapping CSV.
- Create JIRA epic SEC-1045 to track migration tasks and acceptance criteria.
- Stand-up 1hr working session with Platform and SRE to plan pilot tenant onboarding.

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This doc is intentionally prescriptive in areas where we need to move quickly (packaging and signing). Expect more detailed PRDs per subcomponent.
- I left some UX decisions (how roles show in console) for Product to weigh in; these can be orthogonal to authorization logic.
